extracted.intended_audience: researchers and faculty preparing NSF proposals and serving as NSF reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on how NSF proposals are reviewed (merit review) including the National Science Board criteria of Intellectual Merit and Broader Impacts and the five elements used to apply those criteria. Also includes brief best-practice advice for proposers.

rubrics_metrics.name: National Science Board approved review criteria (overarching)
rubrics_metrics.description: All NSF proposals are reviewed according to the National Science Board approved criteria of Intellectual Merit and Broader Impacts. Additional review criteria may be described in the solicitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These criteria are based on merit review principles and are applied through consideration of the five elements (see PAPPG Chapter III.A). See the NSF Proposal & Award Policies & Procedures Guide (PAPPG) and the NSF Merit Review website for full guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual Merit
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the proposed activity will advance knowledge and understanding within its own field or across different fields. Intellectual Merit is one of the two required NSF review criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broader Impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: The potential to benefit society and contribute to the achievement of specific, desired societal outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider how the proposed activity will benefit society or advance desired societal outcomes. Broader Impacts is one of the two required NSF review criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merit review element 1: potential to advance knowledge and benefit society
rubrics_metrics.description: What is the potential for the proposed activity to: Advance knowledge and understanding within its own field or across different fields (Intellectual Merit); and Benefit society or advance desired societal outcomes (Broader Impacts)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This element maps directly to the two overarching criteria; reviewers should evaluate the project's overall potential impact on knowledge and on society.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merit review element 2: creativity and transformative potential
rubrics_metrics.description: To what extent do the proposed activities suggest and explore creative, original, or potentially transformative concepts?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess novelty, originality, and potential for transformational change in concepts, approaches, or understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merit review element 3: quality of plan and assessment mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the plan for carrying out the proposed activities well-reasoned, well-organized, and based on a sound rationale? Does the plan incorporate mechanisms to assess success?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate clarity, organization, rationale, feasibility, and whether the proposal includes appropriate milestones, metrics, or evaluation methods to assess progress and success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merit review element 4: qualifications of personnel and organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: How well qualified is the individual, team, or organization to conduct the proposed activities?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the investigators' track records, complementary expertise, team composition, and organizational capacity to carry out the project successfully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merit review element 5: adequacy of resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Are there adequate resources available to the PI (either at the home organization or through collaborations) to carry out the proposed activities?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate institutional support, facilities, equipment, collaborations, and other resources necessary for project completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional solicitation-specific review criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional review criteria may be described in the solicitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers and proposers must consult the specific funding solicitation for any program-specific criteria or emphasis beyond the two NSF-wide criteria and five elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best practice: include suggested reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Always include suggested reviewers with your application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing suggested reviewers helps the program identify appropriate experts; follow solicitation or PAPPG instructions on how to submit suggested (or non-preferred) reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best practice: contact Program Officers about program fit / co-review
rubrics_metrics.description: If you believe your proposal equally fits in two programs, contact the Program Officers to discuss the best fit. Your work may be a candidate for co-review (i.e. review by more than one program).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early contact with Program Officers can improve routing and ensure the proposal is reviewed by the most appropriate panel(s).
